sections.label: The opening
sections.line: An edition of the book for one person
sections.para: Once the book is a graph, an agent can assemble an edition for one person: their chapters, altitude and examples, later their language, sent as a PDF and not published. The brief can come from the correspondence notes, which stay private. Readers pay as they read, from five pounds of credit, starting in the browser with the vault as an option.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Assembled for one, paid as read
sections.para: An agent assembles an edition from the book's graph for one reader, at their altitude with their examples. It is sent, not published, and its private brief never appears in it. Payment works like the newsroom's meter: five pounds of credit, more read, more paid. It starts locally and can be kept in the reader's vault.

sections.label: An edition for one
sections.line: Walking a different path through the graph
sections.para: A book that is a graph can be assembled by an agent, even a cloud session. Given a person, say a designer moving into product who thinks in pictures and fears AI, the agent picks the chapters that matter, at their altitude, with examples from their world and infographics first, and eventually in their language and culture.

sections.label: The brief is already there
sections.line: The brief exists, and stays private
sections.para: The correspondence agents keep a CRM with a folder per person, what was discussed and where each fact came from, which is what an editor would want before choosing. That folder stays private: the agent reads it to choose, and the edition carries choices, not notes. It goes to that person only, encrypted to their key once the people directory exists.

sections.label: Pay as you read
sections.line: Pay as you read, from five pounds
sections.para: Like the newsroom's articles, the book can be paid as it is read: start with five pounds of credit, pay more the more you read, set the price from free to double, with a balance that can go negative. It applies to personal editions too, starting in the reader's browser with an option to save to their vault.

sections.label: How it would work
sections.line: Six steps from graph to reader
sections.para: The book as a graph at every altitude; a private brief or a reader's form with role, altitude and language; an agent that assembles the edition; a PDF or browser edition sent to that person only; the meter starting at five pounds; and the reader's vault to keep it.

sections.label: How innovation works
sections.para: Dinis knows the book's website is coming and how things are built here, with vaults, graphs, the meter and agents with roles, so he can already build on top of it in a brief. Each thing built becomes something the next idea stands on.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.para: Nothing is built: not the website, the graph or the editions. Personal editions are sent, not published, and the notes behind them stay private. Translation and culture come later; first editions would be in English. Whether people pay for a book this way is what the experiment would show.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: A memo and the newsroom's pieces
sections.para: From Dinis's voice memo of 18 October 2026. Related articles cover the book's website, the book's plan, paying after the value, the agent team that runs his correspondence, and the directory of people and their keys.
